name: LM358DR2G
title: Single supply dual operational amplifiers (LM258, LM358, LM358A, LM2904, LM2904A, LM2904V, NCV2904, NCV2904V)
summary: Dual general-purpose bipolar op amps, internally compensated, for one supply of 3.0 V to 32 V or split supplies up to ±16 V. Both the input common mode range and the output swing reach the negative rail, and the two amplifiers together draw 0.7 mA typical at 5 V. The grades differ in ambient range and in offset, bias and gain limits; LM358DR2G is the 0 to +70°C LM358 in SOIC-8 on reels of 2500.

circuits.title: Voltage reference
circuits.description: An MC1403 makes 2.5 V, which one amplifier buffers and scales up as a non-inverting stage: R1 runs from the output back to the inverting input and R2 from that input to ground, so VO = 2.5 V × (1 + R1/R2). The MC1403 and the amplifier both run from VCC.

circuits.title: Wien bridge oscillator
circuits.description: A sine-wave oscillator on one amplifier and a single supply, with everything referred to Vref, half of VCC. A series R-C from the output and a parallel R-C to Vref form the frequency-setting bridge into the non-inverting input; with R = 16 kΩ and C = 0.01 µF it runs at 1.0 kHz (fo = 1/(2πRC)). Gain comes from 10 kΩ from Vref to the inverting input and 50 kΩ from the output back to it; across the 50 kΩ sits a 5.0 kΩ potentiometer, wired as a variable resistor, in series with two diodes in inverse parallel, which lower the gain as the swing grows.

parts.note: potentiometer; wiper tied to the end on the inverting input

notes: Vref = VCC/2.

circuits.title: High impedance differential amplifier
circuits.description: Three amplifiers make an instrumentation-style differential amplifier: each input, e1 and e2, goes straight to a non-inverting input, so the source sees a high impedance. R1 joins the two inverting inputs and aR1 and bR1 close each loop. The third amplifier takes the difference of the two outputs through resistors of R/C, with R as its feedback and R from its non-inverting input to ground, so eo = C(1 + a + b)(e2 - e1).

circuits.title: Comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: One amplifier switching as a comparator. Vin drives the inverting input; Vref feeds the non-inverting input through R1, and R2 from the output back to that input gives positive feedback. Rising, the output flips at VinH; falling, at VinL; the gap between them is R1/(R1 + R2) of the output swing VOH - VOL.

circuits.title: Bi-quad filter
circuits.description: A state-variable bi-quad from four amplifiers (two packages), every non-inverting input at Vref = VCC/2, giving a bandpass and a notch output. The first amplifier sums the input (through C1 and R2) with the third amplifier's output (through R), and has R in parallel with C as feedback; its output is the bandpass output. The second is an integrator (R in, C feedback); the third inverts its output with a pair of 100 kΩ resistors and closes the loop back to the first. The fourth sums the input (through a second R2) and the bandpass signal (through R1), with R3 as feedback, and its output leaves through a second C1 as the notch output. With R = 160 kΩ, C = 0.001 µF and R1 = R2 = R3 = 1.6 MΩ the centre frequency is 1.0 kHz, Q is 10 and both gains are 1.

parts.note: R, third amplifier output to first amplifier input

notes: TBP is the gain at the centre frequency and TN the passband gain of the notch output.

circuits.title: Function generator
circuits.description: A triangle and square wave generator from two amplifiers, both referred to Vref = VCC/2. The first is an integrator: Rf carries the square wave into its inverting input, C is its feedback and its non-inverting input sits at Vref; its output is the triangle wave. The second is a comparator with hysteresis: the triangle reaches its non-inverting input through R3 (75 kΩ), R1 (100 kΩ) returns that input to Vref and R2 (300 kΩ) feeds back from its output, which is the square wave; its inverting input is at Vref.
notes: 75 kΩ is R1 and R2 in parallel, the condition the frequency equation holds under.

circuits.title: Multiple feedback bandpass filter
circuits.description: A bandpass filter on one amplifier, non-inverting input at Vref = VCC/2. Vin passes R1 into a node that R2 returns to ground; from that node one C goes to the output and the other to the inverting input, and R3 joins the output to the inverting input. CO, ten times C, couples the output to VO. Pick the centre frequency and C, then R3, R1 and R2 follow from Q and the centre-frequency gain.
notes: Where the source impedance changes, a voltage follower in front keeps the filter's response fixed.
The amplifier adds under 10 % error while Qo·fo/BW < 0.1, fo and BW in Hz.

operation.text: Two op amps in one package, built from the same circuit as the company's quad amplifier: an LM358 is half an LM324. The grades differ in ambient range and in offset, bias and gain limits: LM358 and LM358A (0 to +70°C), LM258 (-25 to +85°C), LM2904 and LM2904A (-40 to +105°C), LM2904V and NCV2904 (-40 to +125°C), NCV2904V (-40 to +150°C).
Runs from one supply of 3.0 V to 32 V, or from split supplies. Per amplifier, supply current is roughly a fifth of an MC1741's.
On a single supply, VCC takes 3.0 V up to VCC(max) and VEE/Gnd is ground. On split supplies, VCC is 1.5 V up to VCC(max) above ground and VEE is 1.5 V up to VEE(max) below it.

The input common mode range includes the negative supply, which in many single-supply uses removes the need for external biasing parts, and the output range includes the negative supply too. The input stage is truly differential, with ESD clamps on the inputs that leave normal operation unaffected. Outputs are protected against short circuits and the amplifiers are internally compensated.

Neither input, nor the common mode voltage, may go more than 0.3 V below the negative rail. The top of the common mode range is VCC - 1.7 V. Below a 32 V supply, no input may exceed the supply voltage.

A short from an output to ground is rated continuous, at 40 mA typical and 60 mA maximum. A short from an output to VCC overheats the device and can destroy it, and shorting every amplifier at the same time can dissipate enough to destroy it.

Two internally compensated stages make up each amplifier. Stage one (differential pair Q20/Q18 behind input buffers Q21/Q17, feeding the differential to single-ended converter Q3/Q4) supplies gain, level shift and a reduced transconductance; Q20 and Q18 have split collectors for that reduction, so the compensation capacitor is only 5.0 pF and takes less die area. With the inputs at the negative supply (ground on one supply), neither the input transistors nor the converter saturate. Stage two is a current-source-loaded amplifier.

An internal voltage regulator with a low temperature coefficient biases each amplifier; the bias circuit is shared by both amplifiers. This gives stable behaviour over temperature and high power supply rejection.

Junction-to-air thermal resistance is 238 °C/W for Micro8, 212 °C/W for SOIC-8 and 161 °C/W for PDIP-8, measured on an evaluation board with 1 oz copper and minimum pads, with all outputs active. Junction temperature is limited to 150°C.
NCV2904 and NCV2904V, the NCV-prefixed parts, are AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable, for automotive and other applications that require unique site and change control.
Every part number is lead-free, free of halogens and BFRs, and meets RoHS.
